news.title: Gianni Infantino statement after Argentina letter leaked and FIFA president told to resign
news.lede: The World Cup was undoubtedly a success on the pitch, though issues off the field and at a governing level threatened to overshadow the football more than once. At the centre of all that was FIFA’s president, Gianni Infantino, who even in the final seconds of the World Cup managed to hog the limelight, cutting in front of the Spanish players before their trophy lift in an effort to get USA president Donald Trump off the stage . In addition to the exorbitant ticket pricing, which had sparked anger long before a ball was even kicked, Infantino allowed politics to interfere with the world’s most-watched sporting tournament. FIFA failed to act when one of its most respected referees was denied entry to the United States.

news.title: NFL stadium used to host World Cup games completes major transformation back to football - 'welcome back'
news.lede: SOFI STADIUM has been given a makeover after hosting eight showdowns during the World Cup. The 70,240-capacity arena staged two USA clashes during the tournament, including the group-opening win over Paraguay. And Spain also featured at SoFi Stadium as they beat Belgium en route to being crowned World Cup champions. But the home of the Los Angeles Rams and Los Angeles Chargers is now back in NFL mode ahead of the new season.

news.title: Cape Verde's World Cup hero keeper Vozinha forced to CHANGE NAME to play for next club
news.lede: WORLD CUP hero Vozinha will don a shirt bearing an unfamiliar name at new club Colo-Colo. The Cape Verde goalkeeper, 40, became an overnight star with a string of heroic performances at this summer‘s tournament. Those displays convinced Chilean giants Colo-Colo to snap him up as a free agent – sealing one of the biggest moves of his career. But under current rules the veteran stopper will not be allowed to start the season with ‘Vozinha’ on his back.

news.title: Mitrade Renews Argentina Football Sponsorship Into 2027, Nine Days After World Cup Final Loss
news.lede: Mitrade renewed its sponsorship of the Argentine Football Association into 2027, the CFD trading platform said today (Tuesday). The announcement came nine days after Argentina lost the World Cup final 1-0 to Spain at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey.Mitrade's release describes AFA as home to the three-time world champions, a count this month's tournament left unchanged. Argentina won in 1978, 1986 and 2022. A 2025 Asia Deal Repointed at the GulfWhen the two sides first signed in July 2025, Mitrade pitched the arrangement at Southeast Asia and Australia, saying Argentina jerseys were outselling those of older football powers across the region.The renewal is aimed at the Middle East and North Africa instead.

news.title: Roger Milla: Football's Iconic Smiles at the World Stage
news.lede: Roger Milla, revered as one of football's most iconic figures, continues to be celebrated for his extraordinary contributions on football’s grandest platform. Having played in three World Cups, Milla set enduring records and began trends that persist in modern football. One of the earliest African players to gain prominence in Europe during the 1970s, Milla had initially retired from the national team but made a comeback following a personal appeal from the president of Cameroon. Participating in the 1990 World Cup in Italy at the age of 38, Milla's dynamic performances helped Cameroon become the first African team to reach the World Cup quarterfinals.
